exclusions.reason: The construction needs fresh independent fair bits at every switch, not a compact key.

hypotheses.statement: For each sufficiently small fixed $\bar\eta>0$, choose a sufficiently small $\bar\kappa>0$ with $\bar\kappa<\bar\eta/256$.

 \qquad(d\longrightarrow\infty).$$
The sign representation is annihilated by every nonempty fair layer.
For every fixed dyadic $n\ge2$, $\|B_n(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1$ on every nontrivial irreducible.
For every integer $t\ge0$, $$\|q_d^{*t}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge1-2^{tn/2}/n!.$$
For integers $r\ge s\ge1$ and any matrix $T$, setting $Q=T^*T$, $$\|T^r\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\le\|Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{r-s}\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}Q^s.$$
Uniformly in $n$, $\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}D_\lambda^{-1}$ is bounded, and $$\sum_{\lambda\ne(n),(1^n)}D_\lambda^{-1}\longrightarrow0.$$

For every such $(a,b)$ there is a probability distribution on even densities $R$ such that $$Q_{a,b}\preceq e^{F(a,b)}u(a,b)\,\mathbb E R^{\otimes p}.
 \label{eq:signed-type-density-exact}$$ For every even density $T$ and every type $(a,b)$, $$\|T^{\otimes p}Q_{a,b}\|_{\rm op}\le e^{-F(a,b)}.
 \label{eq:signed-global-density-upper}$$ Moreover $u(a,b)\le(p+1)^{q(q-1)}$.*


*For arbitrary parity dimensions, the upper bound has the following carrier form.
Let $W$ be any set of $p=sm-l$ occupied cells of an $s$-row, $m$-column rectangle.
Let $G$ be finite, let $H\le G$, and let $x=\sum_{g\in G}x_g g$ be positive in $\mathbb C[G]$.
Fix $N\ge p\ge0$, $q\ge1$, and put $B=N+q+1$.
Suppose $x\succeq0$ is in $\mathbb C[S_t]$, $h$ specified points are fixed, and $a,b$ each have at most $q$ parts and total size $t-h$.

There is an absolute $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, if $\lambda\vdash n$ has at most $n/2$ rows and $k=n-\lambda_1\ge1$, then $$\log D_\lambda\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c k\log(n/k),&k\le n/4,\\
 c n,&k\ge n/4.
 \end{cases}$$

There is an absolute $C_0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $\lambda\vdash n$ with at most $n/2$ rows has an occurrence [ten:spin:eq:1] with $l=0$ and $$F(\alpha,\beta)\le C_0\log D_\lambda. \label{ten:spin:eq:4}$$

For $n=2^d$ there is a decision forest whose output is always a permutation of $[n]$, whose input consists of independent fair bits, and whose coordinate trees have depth $O(\log n)$, such that the output law has total variation distance $o(1)$ from uniform as $d\to\infty$.
Let $P_\rho$ be the symmetric-group isotypic projection of shape $\rho\vdash p$ on the signed tensor power $V^{\otimes p}$.
On the board $W$ of Theorem 9, let $P_\gamma$ be a full $S_p$-isotypic projection, and let $P_R,P_C$ be products of full symmetric-group isotypic projections on the occupied row and column sites.
Let $W$ contain $n-t$ occupied cells in an $a$ by $b$ board, $n=ab$.
Let $A,B\succeq0$ and suppose $A\preceq c_A\int A_x\,d\mu(x)$ and $B\preceq c_B\int B_y\,d\nu(y)$, where $c_A,c_B\ge0$, all integrands are positive, and $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures.
Let $\rho_i$ and $\sigma_j$ be trace-one positive matrices indexed by $a$ rows and $b$ columns.
Let $K$ be a compact group, let $\rho$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation on $\mathcal H$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible unitary representation on $\mathcal U$ of dimension $M$.
Let $n=ab\ge4$, where $a,b\ge2$ are powers of two and $|\log_2a-\log_2b|\le1$.
Under the hypotheses of Proposition 22, let $0\le\theta\le1$, let $c$ be real, and let $\mathcal B_a,\mathcal B_b\ge0$.

For the constants fixed above, there are absolute choices of $C_0$ and an integer $h\ge1$ such that, for every dyadic $n\ge2$, every $\lambda\vdash n$, and every occurrence shown below with $m=|\tau|$, $$\lambda\ \text{in}\ \mu*\nu^{\rm t}*\tau
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 W_n(\lambda)
 \le
 \exp\{ \beta_n \mathcal S(\mu,\nu)+ R_n(m)\}.
 \label{ten:named:eq:9}$$

There are absolute constants $c>0$ and $C$ such that, for every dyadic $n\ge2$ and every $\lambda\vdash n$ with $2\le k=n-\lambda_1\le n/2$, $$\|B_n\|_\lambda^2 \le \exp(-c k\log(n/k)+C k),\qquad
                         2\le k\le n/2                     \label{ten:lowering:eq:1}$$ The block with defect one is zero.

Suppose, at a sufficiently large dyadic size $m$, positive numbers $E_\mu$ satisfy $$\log E_\mu\le \beta F(\eta_0)+G_m(m-|\eta_0|)
 \quad\text{for every $q_m$-hook $\eta_0\subseteq\mu$.}
 \label{ten:lowering:eq:4}$$ Then every subdiagram $\eta\subseteq\mu$, of size $m-l$, satisfies $$\log E_\mu\le\beta F(\eta)+G_m(l).
                                                                  \label{ten:lowering:eq:5}$$ The same conclusion is automatic when $E_\mu=0$, with logarithm $-\infty$.

For sufficiently small fixed $b>0$ and then sufficiently small fixed $c>0$, there are a constant $C$ and exponents $p_d\ge2$ with $\sup_{d\ge1}p_d<\infty$ such that, for every $d\ge1$ and every $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$D_\lambda {\rm tr}|\rho_\lambda(B_n)|^{p_d}\le
 \exp\{L_n(\lambda)+C n^{1-c/2}\}.
 \label{ten:compressed:eq:1}$$
There are an absolute threshold $D$ and, after $D$ is fixed, an absolute power of two $p\ge1$ such that the following bounds hold at every level $l\ge0$ and every size $n=2^d$ with $1\le d\le2^lD$.

There are real exponents $p_d\ge2$, with $\sup_{d\ge1}p_d<\infty$, such that for every $d\ge1$ and every $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$\log J_n(\lambda,p_d)\le
 \begin{cases}
 G_n(\lambda),&n-\lambda_1>n^{1-\epsilon},\\
 0,&n-\lambda_1\le n^{1-\epsilon}.
 \end{cases}$$ For all sufficiently large $n$, the second bound strengthens to $\log J_n(\lambda,p_d)\le-10k\log n$ when $1\le k=n-\lambda_1\le n^{1-\epsilon}$.
Say that a diagram fits the $q$-hook if all cells belong to its first $q$ rows or its first $q$ columns.
There are absolute $C$ and $m_0$ with the following property.

There are real exponents $p(d)\ge1$, indexed by integers $d\ge1$, with $\sup_{d\ge1}p(d)<\infty$ such that, for every integer $d\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$D_\lambda\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}|B_n|^{2p(d)}\le e^{E_n^+(\lambda)}.$$

There is a fixed positive integer $p$ such that, simultaneously for every integer $d\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda=(n-k,\beta)\vdash n=2^d$ with $\lambda\ne(n)$ and $\lambda'_1\le n/2$, where $k=n-\lambda_1\ge1$, $$\begin{aligned}
 \log T_n^\lambda(p)&\le
 k\log n\left(u_d-\Lambda
          \left(\frac{\log(n/k)}{\log n}\right)^2\right),
       \label{rec:hybrid-level-budget}\\
 \log T_n^\lambda(p)&\le\mathcal D_d(\lambda).
       \label{rec:hybrid-diagram-budget}
\end{aligned}$$ If $\log(n/k)/\log n\ge\epsilon$, the first bound is at most $-k\log n$.

outputs.exact_statement: For each sufficiently small fixed $\bar\eta>0$, choose a sufficiently small $\bar\kappa>0$ with $\bar\kappa<\bar\eta/256$. There is an integer $r\ge1$, depending only on these fixed constants, such that for every $d\ge1$, every $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, and every occurrence [ten:spin:eq:1], $$\label{ten:spin:eq:3} \log\!\left(D_\lambda\operatorname{Tr}_{V_\lambda}(B_n^*B_n)^r\right) \le\eta_d F(\alpha,\beta)+g_n(l),$$ where $$\eta_d=\bar\eta\left(1-\frac1{2\sqrt d}\right),\qquad \kappa_d=\bar\kappa\left(1-\frac1{2\sqrt d}\right),\qquad g_n(l)=\max\{0,\kappa_d l\log n-l\log(n/l)\}.$$ Set $g_n(0)=0$ and interpret the logarithm of a zero trace as $-\infty$.

There is an absolute positive integer $L$ such that $$\mathbb E_{U_{S_n}}|f_{d,L}-1|^2\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(d\longrightarrow\infty).$$ The convergence is uniform over starting orders. Moreover $t_{\mathrm{mix}}(d)=\Theta(d)$.
The sign representation is annihilated by every nonempty fair layer. Every irreducible of $S_n$ indexed by a shape with more than $n/2$ rows is annihilated by a sweep.
For every fixed dyadic $n\ge2$, $\|B_n(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1$ on every nontrivial irreducible.
For every integer $t\ge0$, $$\|q_d^{*t}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge1-2^{tn/2}/n!.$$ Consequently $t_{\mathrm{mix}}(d)\ge\lceil(2/n)\log_2(3n!/4)\rceil=2d-O(1)$.
For integers $r\ge s\ge1$ and any matrix $T$, setting $Q=T^*T$, $$\|T^r\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\le\|Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{r-s}\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}Q^s.$$

Uniformly in $n$, $\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}D_\lambda^{-1}$ is bounded, and $$\sum_{\lambda\ne(n),(1^n)}D_\lambda^{-1}\longrightarrow0.$$ If $\ell=n-\max(\lambda_1,\lambda'_1)$, then $$\log D_\lambda\ge(\log2)\sqrt\ell/2,
 \qquad \sup_n\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}D_\lambda^{-32}<\infty.$$

For every such $(a,b)$ there is a probability distribution on even densities $R$ such that $$Q_{a,b}\preceq e^{F(a,b)}u(a,b)\,\mathbb E R^{\otimes p}.
 \label{eq:signed-type-density-exact}$$ For every even density $T$ and every type $(a,b)$, $$\|T^{\otimes p}Q_{a,b}\|_{\rm op}\le e^{-F(a,b)}.
 \label{eq:signed-global-density-upper}$$ Moreover $u(a,b)\le(p+1)^{q(q-1)}$.*


*For arbitrary parity dimensions, the upper bound has the following carrier form. Let $E_+=\mathbb C^{r_+}$ and $E_-=\mathbb C^{r_-}$, for nonnegative integers $r_+,r_-$, and let $a,b$ have at most $r_+,r_-$ parts, respectively, with $|a|+|b|=p$. Write $\mathbf S_a(E_+)$ and $\mathbf S_b(E_-)$ for the ordinary polynomial carriers of highest weights $a,b$. For a positive parity-preserving matrix $T$ on $E_+\oplus E_-$, let its induced carrier action be $\pi_{a,b}(T)=\mathbf S_a(T|_{E_+})\otimes\mathbf S_b(T|_{E_-})$. With $F(a,b)$ given by the same entropy formula, $$\|\pi_{a,b}(T)\|_{\rm op}
 \le (\operatorname{Tr}T)^p e^{-F(a,b)}.
 \label{eq:signed-carrier-density-upper}$$ A zero-dimensional factor has the empty partition and contributes the scalar identity. If $p=0$, then $\pi_{a,b}(T)=1$ and the right-hand side is interpreted as one, even when $\operatorname{Tr}T=0$.

Let $G$ be finite, let $H\le G$, and let $x=\sum_{g\in G}x_g g$ be positive in $\mathbb C[G]$. Set $E_Hx=\sum_{h\in H}x_hh$. For $\rho\in\widehat H$ let $\Lambda_\rho$ be the set of $\mu\in\widehat G$ whose restriction to $H$ contains $\rho$. With $d_\rho=\dim\rho$ and $d_\mu=\dim\mu$, $$0\le\operatorname{Tr}_\rho(E_Hx)
 \le\frac1{[G:H]d_\rho}
       \sum_{\mu\in\Lambda_\rho}d_\mu\operatorname{Tr}_\mu(x).
 \label{eq:pointwise-positive-restriction}$$ For $G=S_s$ and $H=S_{s-h}$ fixing $h$ specified points, the index is $(s)_h=s!/(s-h)!$.

Fix $N\ge p\ge0$, $q\ge1$, and put $B=N+q+1$. If $V_\rho$ occurs in $\mathcal M_{a,b}$ from [eq:signed-sector-decomposition], then $\rho_{q+1}\le q$ and $$e^{F(a,b)}B^{-7q^2}\le D_\rho, \qquad \dim\mathcal M_{a,b}\le e^{F(a,b)}. \label{eq:hook-dimension-explicit}$$ The multiplicity of any $V_\rho$ in $V^{\otimes p}$ is at most $B^{10q^2}$. The occurring shapes are exactly the $(q,q)$-hook shapes. There are at most $(p+1)^{2q}$ such shapes.

Suppose $x\succeq0$ is in $\mathbb C[S_t]$, $h$ specified points are fixed, and $a,b$ each have at most $q$ parts and total size $t-h$. Fix an arbitrary real scalar $G$. Assume, for every $\mu\vdash t$ extending a constituent of $\mathcal M_{a,b}$, $$D_\mu\operatorname{Tr}_\mu x
 \le \exp\{\eta F(a,b)+G\},\qquad 0\le\eta\le1.$$ Write $\mathsf p(t)$ for the number of partitions of $t$, and let $B=N+q+1$ with $N\ge t$. Then $$\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{a,b}E_{S_{t-h}}x)
 \le \frac{\mathsf p(t)}{(t)_h}
    B^{15q^2}\exp\{-(1-\eta)F(a,b)+G\}.
 \label{eq:local-stabilizer-trace-explicit}$$

There is an absolute $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, if $\lambda\vdash n$ has at most $n/2$ rows and $k=n-\lambda_1\ge1$, then $$\log D_\lambda\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c k\log(n/k),&k\le n/4,\\
 c n,&k\ge n/4.
 \end{cases}$$

There is an absolute $C_0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $\lambda\vdash n$ with at most $n/2$ rows has an occurrence [ten:spin:eq:1] with $l=0$ and $$F(\alpha,\beta)\le C_0\log D_\lambda. \label{ten:spin:eq:4}$$

For $n=2^d$ there is a decision forest whose output is always a permutation of $[n]$, whose input consists of independent fair bits, and whose coordinate trees have depth $O(\log n)$, such that the output law has total variation distance $o(1)$ from uniform as $d\to\infty$. The same conclusion holds with independent uniform $[n]$-valued input cells.

Let $P_\rho$ be the symmetric-group isotypic projection of shape $\rho\vdash p$ on the signed tensor power $V^{\otimes p}$. There is a probability distribution on even densities such that $$P_\rho\preceq D_\rho B^{10q^2}\mathbb E R^{\otimes p},
 \qquad B=N+q+1,\quad N\ge p.
 \label{eq:signed-isotypic-density}$$ If $P_\rho=0$, the assertion is read with any density distribution.

On the board $W$ of Theorem 9, let $P_\gamma$ be a full $S_p$-isotypic projection, and let $P_R,P_C$ be products of full symmetric-group isotypic projections on the occupied row and column sites. Write their diagrams as $\rho_i$ and $\sigma_j$, and set $D_R=\prod_iD_{\rho_i}$, $D_C=\prod_jD_{\sigma_j}$. With $N=sm$ and $B=N+q+1$, $$\|P_C P_\gamma P_R\|_{\rm op}^2 \le\min\left\{1, \frac{D_RD_C}{D_\gamma}B^{10(s+m)q^2}e^l\right\}. \label{eq:signed-isotypic-angle}$$ Empty blocks use the trivial partition and dimension one. The conclusion is uniform over the location of the $l$ missing cells.

Let $W$ contain $n-t$ occupied cells in an $a$ by $b$ board, $n=ab$. Assume $\omega\vdash n-t$ and every prescribed row and column type $\eta_g$ are $(q,q)$-hook shapes: their $(q+1)$st part is at most $q$. Here $1\le q\le n$. Suppose $X=\prod_{g\text{ row}}X_g$ and $Y=\prod_{g\text{ column}}Y_g$ are positive group-algebra elements, with each $X_g,Y_g$ supported on the indicated local type. Write $c_g$ for its unnormalized trace on one copy of $V_{\eta_g}$ and $S=\sum_g\log D_{\eta_g}$. Then $$\operatorname{Tr}_{\omega}(XY)
 \le\Bigl(\prod_g c_g\Bigr)
 \exp\{C(a+b+1)q^2\log(n+1)+t
                  +\min(0,S-\log D_\omega)\}.$$ The constant is absolute. On the $\omega$-isotypic part of the signed tensor power, the same bound is multiplied by its multiplicity $w_\omega$.

Let $A,B\succeq0$ and suppose $A\preceq c_A\int A_x\,d\mu(x)$ and $B\preceq c_B\int B_y\,d\nu(y)$, where $c_A,c_B\ge0$, all integrands are positive, and $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures. Then, for every $P$, $$\|A^{1/2}PB^{1/2}\|\le\sqrt{c_Ac_B}\sup_{x,y}\|A_x^{1/2}PB_y^{1/2}\|.$$

Let $\rho_i$ and $\sigma_j$ be trace-one positive matrices indexed by $a$ rows and $b$ columns. Put $\bar\rho=a^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i$ and use its inverse on its support. For a unitary $U$ set $$z_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}(\bar\rho^{-1/2}\rho_i\bar\rho^{-1/2}U\sigma_jU^*)\ge0.$$ Then $\sum_{i,j}z_{ij}\le ab$. On any $ab-t$ occupied cells their product is at most $e^t$.

Let $K$ be a compact group, let $\rho$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation on $\mathcal H$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible unitary representation on $\mathcal U$ of dimension $M$. Identify the $\pi$-isotypic subspace with $\mathcal U\otimes\mathcal M$. For $A\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal U)$, let $\widetilde A$ act there as $A\otimes I_{\mathcal M}$ and be zero on all other isotypes. With normalized Haar measure, $$\widetilde A=\int_K f_A(g)\rho(g)\,dg,
 \qquad f_A(g)=M\operatorname{Tr}(A\pi(g)^*),$$ and $$\int_K|f_A(g)|\,dg
 \le\sqrt M\,\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
 \le M\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$ If the type does not occur, $\widetilde A=0$ and the same identity holds.

Under the hypotheses of Proposition 22, let $0\le\theta\le1$, let $c$ be real, and let $\mathcal B_a,\mathcal B_b\ge0$. Suppose that, for $m\in\{a,b\}$, every $\xi\vdash m$ and every $q$-hook $\eta\subseteq\xi$, with $l=m-|\eta|$, satisfy $$E_m(\xi;p)\le \mathcal B_m+\theta H_\eta+c\,l\log m-j_m(l). \label{s:eq:inverse-child-budget}$$ Then every prescribed $q$-hook $\omega\subseteq\lambda$, with $t=n-|\omega|$, satisfies $$\begin{aligned} E_n(\lambda;p) &\le\theta H_\omega+c\,t\log n-j_n(t)+a\mathcal B_b+b\mathcal B_a\notag\\ &\hspace{9mm}+C\left[t+(a+b)(q^2+n^{1/4})\log(n+1)\right]. \label{s:eq:inverse-budget-specialization} \end{aligned}$$ The constant $C$ does not depend on $p,q,\theta,c,\mathcal B_a,\mathcal B_b$.

For the constants fixed above, there are absolute choices of $C_0$ and an integer $h\ge1$ such that, for every dyadic $n\ge2$, every $\lambda\vdash n$, and every occurrence shown below with $m=|\tau|$, $$\lambda\ \text{in}\ \mu*\nu^{\rm t}*\tau
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 W_n(\lambda)
 \le
 \exp\{ \beta_n \mathcal S(\mu,\nu)+ R_n(m)\}.
 \label{ten:named:eq:9}$$

There are absolute constants $c>0$ and $C$ such that, for every dyadic $n\ge2$ and every $\lambda\vdash n$ with $2\le k=n-\lambda_1\le n/2$, $$\|B_n\|_\lambda^2 \le \exp(-c k\log(n/k)+C k),\qquad
                         2\le k\le n/2                     \label{ten:lowering:eq:1}$$ The block with defect one is zero.

Suppose, at a sufficiently large dyadic size $m$, positive numbers $E_\mu$ satisfy $$\log E_\mu\le \beta F(\eta_0)+G_m(m-|\eta_0|)
 \quad\text{for every $q_m$-hook $\eta_0\subseteq\mu$.}
 \label{ten:lowering:eq:4}$$ Then every subdiagram $\eta\subseteq\mu$, of size $m-l$, satisfies $$\log E_\mu\le\beta F(\eta)+G_m(l).
                                                                  \label{ten:lowering:eq:5}$$ The same conclusion is automatic when $E_\mu=0$, with logarithm $-\infty$.

For sufficiently small fixed $b>0$ and then sufficiently small fixed $c>0$, there are a constant $C$ and exponents $p_d\ge2$ with $\sup_{d\ge1}p_d<\infty$ such that, for every $d\ge1$ and every $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$D_\lambda {\rm tr}|\rho_\lambda(B_n)|^{p_d}\le
 \exp\{L_n(\lambda)+C n^{1-c/2}\}.
 \label{ten:compressed:eq:1}$$

There are an absolute threshold $D$ and, after $D$ is fixed, an absolute power of two $p\ge1$ such that the following bounds hold at every level $l\ge0$ and every size $n=2^d$ with $1\le d\le2^lD$. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with positive trace, (G) holds. For every such $\lambda$ and every $\mu\subseteq\lambda$ with $\mu_{K_n+1}\le K_n$, put $t=n-|\mu|$. If $t>0$ and $\log(n/t)\le u\log n$, then (H) holds: $$\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{(G)} & e_\lambda\le A_l B_\lambda,\\
 \text{(H)} & e_\lambda+J(t,n)\le A_l B_\mu+b_l W(t,n).
 \end{array}                                                         \label{ten:simultaneous:eq:8}$$

There are real exponents $p_d\ge2$, with $\sup_{d\ge1}p_d<\infty$, such that for every $d\ge1$ and every $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$\log J_n(\lambda,p_d)\le
 \begin{cases}
 G_n(\lambda),&n-\lambda_1>n^{1-\epsilon},\\
 0,&n-\lambda_1\le n^{1-\epsilon}.
 \end{cases}$$ For all sufficiently large $n$, the second bound strengthens to $\log J_n(\lambda,p_d)\le-10k\log n$ when $1\le k=n-\lambda_1\le n^{1-\epsilon}$.

Say that a diagram fits the $q$-hook if all cells belong to its first $q$ rows or its first $q$ columns. Write $e_m(l)=l\log(m/l)$, with $e_m(0)=0$. Fix $\theta=1/2$, $c_0=1/100$. Consider $n=ab\ge2$, where $a,b$ are powers of two with $\log_2 a,\log_2 b$ differing by at most one, and $q\le n^{1/16}$ a positive integer. Let $p\ge2$ be real and let $\mathcal B_a,\mathcal B_b\ge0$. Suppose that, for each $m\in\{a,b\}$, every diagram $\xi\vdash m$, and every $q$-hook subdiagram $\eta\subseteq\xi$ of size $m-l$, $$\log J_m(\xi,p)\le \mathcal B_m+\theta H_\eta+c_0\log(m)l-e_m(l),
 \label{ten:inverse:eq:2}$$ using $-\infty$ for log zero. Then for every $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $q$-hook subdiagram $\omega\subseteq\lambda$ of size $g=n-t$, $$\log J_n(\lambda,p)
 \le \theta H_\omega+c_0\log(n)t-e_n(t)+
 a\mathcal B_b+b\mathcal B_a+O\big(t+(a+b)(q^2+n^{1/4})\log(n+1)\big),
 \label{ten:inverse:eq:3}$$ The implicit constant is absolute.

There are absolute $C$ and $m_0$ with the following property. Let $m\ge m_0$ be a power of two and let $p\ge2$. Suppose $$E_m(\xi;p)\le G_m(\xi)\quad\hbox{for large-level $\xi$},
 \qquad
 E_m(\xi;p)\le0\quad\hbox{for the other $\xi$}.$$ Then, for every $\xi\vdash m$ and every subpartition $\eta\subseteq\xi$, putting $l=m-|\eta|$ gives $$E_m(\xi;p)
 \le \mathcal B_m+\theta H_\eta+c_0l\log m-j_m(l),
 \qquad \mathcal B_m=Cm^{1-4\epsilon}\log(m+1).
 \label{s:eq:arbitrary-hook-child-allowance}$$ This includes every $q$-hook subpartition, for any inherited $q\ge1$. The constants do not depend on $p$ or $q$.

There are real exponents $p(d)\ge1$, indexed by integers $d\ge1$, with $\sup_{d\ge1}p(d)<\infty$ such that, for every integer $d\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash n=2^d$, $$D_\lambda\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}|B_n|^{2p(d)}\le e^{E_n^+(\lambda)}.$$ There is a fixed integer $d_*\ge1$ above which one may take $$p(d)=(1+d^{-1/2})
       \max\{p(\lfloor d/2\rfloor),p(\lceil d/2\rceil)\}.$$ In particular $E_n^+\le aW_\lambda$ yields a fixed negative power of $D_\lambda$ for the sweep norm.

There is a fixed positive integer $p$ such that, simultaneously for every integer $d\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda=(n-k,\beta)\vdash n=2^d$ with $\lambda\ne(n)$ and $\lambda'_1\le n/2$, where $k=n-\lambda_1\ge1$, $$\begin{aligned}
 \log T_n^\lambda(p)&\le
 k\log n\left(u_d-\Lambda
          \left(\frac{\log(n/k)}{\log n}\right)^2\right),
       \label{rec:hybrid-level-budget}\\
 \log T_n^\lambda(p)&\le\mathcal D_d(\lambda).
       \label{rec:hybrid-diagram-budget}
\end{aligned}$$ If $\log(n/k)/\log n\ge\epsilon$, the first bound is at most $-k\log n$. For all sufficiently large $d$, in the complementary range, $\mathcal D_d(\lambda)\le\tfrac14\log D_\lambda$.

title: Signed tensor densities and diagram budgets for the Thorp shuffle
